svg.text: Product Service on AWS: containerized microservices with Aurora Global Database disaster recovery
Region A (us-east-1) serves users; Region B (us-west-2) is a pilot light: one task and a read-only database, ready to take over. Written for a demo: one NAT gateway, single-instance clusters.
Terraform switches (off by default in the code)
With all four on, this is the design that was applied and drilled on 2026-11-07
Security groups: internet to ALB (443, 80) to tasks (3000) to database (5432)
Tasks read the secret at runtime with a task role that can read only that secret
HTTP 3000, TLS ends at the ALB
TLS 1.3 at the load balancer; ACM certificate per Region
Tasks: private, non-root, read-only filesystem, no secret in
the environment; the task role can read only one secret
IAM roles trust only ECS in this account (confused deputy)
DB password rotated every 7 days, replicated to Region B
CI per pull request: secret scan, Semgrep, CodeQL, Trivy,
Checkov, npm audit; the image is scanned again weekly
Logs: ALB access logs to a private S3 bucket, CloudWatch
Same posture as Region A: private tasks behind a NAT gateway; the
task role can read only the replica of the database secret
measured: 0 rows lost at about 520 writes/s;
lag at most 0.7 s; writer ready in 31 to 38 s
What the drills measured (2026-11-07, Region A to Region B)
writer ready in Region B 31 to 38 s after the command; 0 rows lost (20,764 acknowledged, 20,764 present)
Main name moved to Region B:
42 to 56 s when Region A's tasks are gone; about 3 min when they run but fail health checks
Planned switchover to Region B and back:
56 s and 53 s; about 32 s of failed reads on the main name (open item)
104 s with no failed request; the first run found and fixed a retry livelock
refused for 13 min 20 s while AWS resynced the old primary; then 59 s
Details, evidence and every issue found:
docs/DR_Test_Results.md | plan and design: docs/DR_Runbook.md, docs/DR_Design_Decisions.md
request and data path inside a Region
disaster recovery: failover record and replication
secret rotation (control plane, no database login)
Region A serves all traffic. Route 53 sends the main name to Region B only when Region A's
targets or its alarm-fed health check turn unhealthy. Both load balancers admit only the
owner's address by default; the API has no authentication, so that restriction is the guard.
Icons: AWS Architecture Icons (07/31/2026 release), used unmodified and resized only.
